cmd-config|description: -# *Secret commands make it so only you can see them when using them, even if they are used in a public channel. This is useful for preventing spam or for testing commands without bothering other users.
links|description: Here are some useful links related to Kami.
help|description: This command is used to get help on the commands available in Kami.
By using /help, you will receive a list of all available commands.
Select the command you wish to know more about to get a detailed description, usage examples, and additional information about that specific command.
If you have any questions or need further assistance, do not hesitate to contact our support team using the /suporte command or by visiting our support server, link available in /links.
help|buttonroll-description: This command creates a message in Discord, where each set of dice listed is presented in a clickable button.
The 'dice' argument must be a string containing the sets of dice you wish to roll. Sets must be separated by the character ´|´.
- **Maximum:** You can add up to 25 sets of dice per command.
help|roll-description: This command allows advanced dice rolling.
Command Format: /roll <dice>
The <dice> argument must contain the dice you wish to roll.
--- Usage Examples ---
1. Basic Roll: To roll a standard dice (ex: a d20).
Example: /roll 1d20
Result: Rolls a single 20-sided dice.
2. Multiple Simple Dice: To roll multiple dice rolls or sum multiple types of dice.
Example: /roll 3d6 + 2d8
Result: Rolls 3 6-sided dice and sums the result with 2 8-sided dice.
3. Roll with Mathematical Operations: Allows including basic operations like multiplication, division, etc.
Example: /roll 2d6 * 3 - 5
Result: Rolls 2d6, multiplies the result by 3, and subtracts 5.
4. Rolling with Modifiers: Use these modifiers to simulate specific rules:
Advantage: Add 'v' to roll the maximum value between two dice.
Example: /roll 2d20v
Disadvantage: Add 'd' to roll the minimum value between two dice.
Example: /roll 2d20d
Greater than (>): To roll a value that must be greater than a specific number.
Example: /roll 2d10>5
Less than (<): To roll a value that must be less than a specific number.
Example: /roll 2d10<5
help|botinfo-description: This command displays a detailed panel with various statistics about the bot's internal operation. It is useful for monitoring and diagnostics.
The info panel contains technical data about the bot's performance and history.
1. Latency (Ping): Indicates the bot's response speed and connection to the database. Lower values are better.
2. Resource Usage (CPU/Memory): Shows current processing and RAM consumption. Indicates if the bot is operating within normal server limits.
3. Uptime: Informs how long the bot has been online and continuously running.
4. Command Statistics: Presents the total number of existing commands and how many commands have been used in the last 24 hours.
help|config-description: This is a configuration command. It allows users to control which groups of bot features and secret commands are active or inactive.
1. Secret General Commands: Makes general BOT commands executed by you invisible to other users.
2. Secret Insanity Commands: Makes insanity-related commands executed by you invisible to other users.
3. Secret Dice Commands (Roll): Makes dice rolling commands executed by you invisible to other users.
4. Secret Sheet Sending Commands: Makes sheet sending commands executed by you invisible to other users.
5. Secret Sheet Creation/Editing Commands: Makes sheet creation and editing commands executed by you invisible to other users.
When executing the command, you will see buttons. Click the buttons to toggle the status (Enable/Disable) of any feature; changes are saved automatically.
There is a specific button to change the bot's operating language (Portuguese or English).
help|links-description: This command displays a panel with useful links related to the Kami BOT.
The links panel contains shortcuts to important resources related to the Kami BOT.
1. Official Website: Link to the official Kami site, where you can find detailed information, documentation, and other functionalities.
2. Invite to Kami: Link to invite Kami to your Discord server.
3. Support Server: Link to the Kami support server, where you can get help, report problems, or suggest improvements directly to the development team.
4. Terms of Use: Link to the Kami terms of use, where you can read about the rules and guidelines for using the bot.
5. Privacy Policy: Link to the Kami privacy policy, where you can understand how your data is collected, used, and protected by the Kami team.
help|support-description: This command is used to contact the Kami BOT support team.
1. message: The message you wish to send to the support team. Describe your problem, question, or suggestion clearly and in detail so that the team can assist you in the best possible way.
--- What happens when you use this command? ---

When sending your message, it will be forwarded to the Kami support team. You will receive a confirmation that your message has been sent successfully. The support team will analyze your message and respond as soon as possible. If you need further assistance, you can use this command again or contact us directly through the support server, whose link is available in the /links command.
help|insanity-description: This command is used to apply an 'insanity' status to a character, simulating the impact of mental conditions or narrative flaws in the game.
You must specify the desired insanity type between Temporary or Permanent.
1. Temporary: Used when the character's mental condition is temporary. The result may vary in the number of applied effects (1, 2, or 3), depending on random variation.
2. Permanent: Used when the condition is considered a fixed trait or a lasting trauma for the character.
To apply a temporary condition: /insanidade temporary
To apply a fixed/trait condition: /insanidade permanent
The result will show the specific insanity terms defined in the database for the chosen type, describing how the character is affected.
help|sheet_configure_password-descriptio: This command is used to configure or change the access password for a character sheet.
1. Sheet Name: The exact name of the character sheet you want to protect (ex: 'Main Character').
2. New Password: The password that will be set to protect the sheet's access.
By executing this command, the system will encrypt the new password and associate it with the specified sheet.
Important: This process changes the sheet's access. If a password is set **and the sheet is set to private**, only those who know the password can view the sheet.
help|sheet_configure_access-description: This command controls the visibility of your character sheet, defining whether it will be publicly accessible or remain restricted by password.
1. Sheet Name: The exact name of the sheet you wish to modify (ex: 'Player Avatar').
2. Visibility: Choose between 'Public' (visible to all) or 'Private' (visible only with password).
By executing the command, the bot will update the sheet's privacy, changing its access status.
Important: If you set the sheet to 'Private', only those who know the password can view it. If you set it to 'Public', anyone with your username can view it.
help|delete_sheet-description: This command allows you to completely delete a sheet you created.
1. Sheet Name: The exact name of the sheet you wish to delete.
**WARNING: This is an irreversible command. Sheet deletion is permanent.**
1. After typing the sheet name, you will be asked to confirm deletion via buttons.
2. Click the CONFIRM button to delete the sheet.
3. If you click CANCEL, the sheet will remain intact.
The system will only allow deletion of sheets belonging to you.
help|sheets_list-description: This command displays a complete list of all sheets you have created and that are associated with your profile.
Does not require additional arguments, as it will search for all sheets linked to the user who executed the command.

The result will be presented in an Embed, listing the name of each sheet on a separate line. If no sheets are found, an informative message will be displayed indicating that you do not have any registered sheets.
help|rename_sheet-description: This command allows you to change the name of a character sheet you created.
1. Sheet Name: The current name of the sheet you wish to change (This field has autocompletion).
2. New Sheet Name: The name you want to give the sheet.
1. You must specify the *current* name of the sheet and the desired *new* name.
2. If the sheet already has the new name, the command will do nothing.
3. If another sheet with the 'New Name' already exists, the command will display an error message.
Upon execution, the bot will ask for confirmation via buttons. If you confirm, the sheet will be renamed, and all internal records will be updated to reflect the new name.
help|sheet_view-description: This command is used to view a specific user's character sheet.
1. Username: The username of the owner of the sheet you wish to view (ex: 'Player123'). It is also possible to use the Discord/Kami Site User ID or mention (@Player123).
2. Sheet Name: The name of the sheet you wish to view (ex: 'Hero Sheet').
3. Password (optional): If the sheet is private, you must provide the correct password to access it.

Upon execution, the bot will try to locate the specified sheet. If the sheet is public, it will be displayed immediately. If it is private, the bot will verify the provided password, and if correct, grant access to the sheet.
help|sheet_send-description: This command transforms a character sheet stored in the system into a formatted Discord message, using embeds. Ideal for sending the complete sheet to other users.
1. Sheet Name: The exact name of the sheet you want to publish (This field has autocompletion).
2. Options (Optional): Defines the sending message behavior.
- Selecting 'Keep message synchronized with the sheet': The bot will send the sheet and add a button to deactivate the synchronization feature.

- If synchronization is active, the message will update automatically whenever the sheet is edited. If the sheet is edited while synchronization is active, the bot will try to update the sent message. If the synchronized message limit is reached, the bot will block sending and inform the user (limit of 3 synchronized messages per sheet).
It is mandatory that the sheet was created by you; sheets from other users can be viewed using the /ficha_ver command, but cannot be sent to the chat using this command.
help|sheet-description: This command is the main one for sheet manipulation, allowing both the creation of new sheets and the addition and editing of attributes within them.
1. Sheet Name: The unique name the sheet will have. (Use autocompletion to check for existing names).
2. Component Type: Defines the data structure (Text, Number, Image, List, Bar). This is crucial, as it defines the format that the 'Value' must follow.
3. Section: The name of the section where the attribute will be added/edited.
4. Attribute: The specific name of the attribute within the section.
5. Value: The content of the attribute. The format of this value MUST correspond to the chosen Component Type.
6. Position (Optional): Defines the exact order of the attribute on the sheet (Format: Section|Number).
• Text/Number/Image: Simply the content in plain text.
• List: Use the format 'add: <quantity> | <item text>' (Ex: add: 1 | New item). To remove use 'del: <item text>', autocompletion will suggest existing items.

• Progress Bar: Use the plus (+) sign to increment, the minus (-) sign to decrement, or a full value in the 'current/max' format to modify (Ex: +5, -10, or 50/100). Autocompletion will also provide suggestions for existing values.
Tip: Using autocompletion is highly recommended to ensure the correct syntax for Section and Attribute names.

The complex syntax is necessary to ensure functionality with the most advanced sheets on the [Kami Site](https://kamiapp.com.br), allowing total flexibility in sheet creation and editing, but it can be a bit difficult to use at first. If you have questions on how to format the arguments, feel free to ask for help using the /suporte command or by joining our support server.
help|sheet_delete_attribute-description: This command removes a specific attribute within a Section of a character sheet.
1. Sheet Name: The sheet from which the attribute will be deleted.
2. Section: The section where the attribute is located (Ex: 'Powers', 'Information').
3. Attribute: The exact name of the attribute you want to remove.
1. The bot first validates whether the sheet belongs to you and if the attribute and section exist.
2. You will receive a confirmation message with buttons. Click 'Confirm' to execute the deletion.
3. After confirmation, the attribute will be removed from the sheet's structure and the system will be synchronized.

This action is irreversible. Make sure you are deleting the correct attribute; the attribute can be added again using the /ficha command if you only want to edit it, or it can be renamed using the /ficha_renomear_atributo command if you only want to change its name.
help|sheet_rename_attribute-description: This command is used to change the name of a specific attribute within a sheet section, without changing its data or position.
1. Sheet Name: The name of the sheet to be modified.
2. Section: The section containing the attribute to be renamed.
3. Attribute: The current name of the attribute.
4. New Name: The name you want to give the attribute.
• The bot verifies if the original attribute actually exists in the specified section.
• The bot checks if the 'New Name' is not already in use by another attribute in the same section (to prevent duplicates).
• You will receive a confirmation message with buttons. It is mandatory to click 'Confirm' to finalize the renaming.
If the 'New Name' already exists, the command will fail and report the duplicate name error. The information contained in the attribute (value, type) is preserved.
help|sheet_rename_section-description: This command allows renaming an entire Section within the structure of a character sheet.
1. Sheet Name: The target sheet for modification.
2. Section: The current name of the section you wish to rename.
3. New Name: The name the section will have after the change.
• The system verifies if the original Section and the New Name are valid.
• The command prevents the creation of duplicate names (the Section cannot receive a name that already exists in another section of the sheet).
• Like other modification commands, the change is confirmed via buttons.
All entries (attributes and values) belonging to this section REMAIN intact; only the visible name of the section will be changed.
help|sheet_delete_section-description: This command removes an entire Section (a block of attributes) from a character sheet. All attributes contained within it will be deleted together.
1. Sheet Name: The target sheet for modification.
2. Section: The exact name of the section you wish to delete. (Must exist on the sheet and belong to you).
• The system confirms that you own the sheet and that the Section exists.
• You will receive a confirmation message with buttons. Click 'Confirm' to execute the deletion.
• **Deletion is permanent. All attributes and values contained in the removed section will be lost.**
This command is more comprehensive than deleting an attribute, as it deletes the entire block of content from the Section.
help|help-description: This command is the central access point for help. It lists all functional bot commands in a single interactive panel.
1. Upon execution, an interactive menu will be displayed, listing all active commands (ex: Sheet, Roll, etc.).
2. You must select the desired command from the dropdown menu.
3. Upon selection, the original panel will be replaced by a detailed Embed, showing the specific description of the chosen command, facilitating easy start of use.
Quick Links: The panel also includes buttons to access the official website and the Kami support page.
Tip: Use this command whenever you are unsure which command to use or what the correct syntax for a feature is.
